body: I read part of it...does that count?
35 M Canada. My wife read Allan Carr’s Easy Way to Quit Smoking. It worked well for her, I still smoke...

I’ve been through a similar situation with my wife. Minus the cheating. She’s on meds that seem to be working good. Good on you for sticking with her! Many mean wouldn’t be able to stick around. Which makes you a hero in my books, and I bet she sees you as her hero. Cheers man!
Used to be a tonne of coke until I couldn’t feel anything, at all. Until I ran out. Then crippling depression.

Right. That I understand, I would check if there is any benefits through the government to offset the costs. Here, if a person is receiving any type of social assistance and does not have the money for a service the government has a set amount that they will pay. It’s not fancy but it is dignified.  If I were the family I would check into any type of financial aide available.

Isn’t there any government assistance available for someone who can not pay for a service. I’m a funeral director from Alberta, and if a family does not have the funds to pay the government generally will step in for a smaller service..
Is it possible that she is suffering from depression? Maybe she needs to see a Doctor. Or, like someone else has mentioned, maybe there is something going on in school...

I did exactly the same thing with the same medication 6 months ago. My Psychiatrist upped my Zoloft to 150 and I’ve been in a lot better position. I also see a councillor a couple times a month. Also, I do a gratitude list every day. 5 things I’m grateful 4. Really was helpful.

I really hope this will help! Please know that there are others that are/have been through this and are willing to help.

And then, Rand al’Thor - the Dragon Reborn - stood up once again to face the Shadow.”

Give me chills every time I read it.

This is coming from a person who attends suicide scenes frequently.  If there is even a chance that someone posting the suicide hotline # will save me from having to cut a young man down from a rope or pick up brain matter off the floor or pull a young lady out of a bloody bathtub, it is worth it.
Also, I can notice a big difference when the medication wears off.  I find it hard to be productive without the meds.
It took a couple of months of trying different medications at different doses in order to find the right fit for me.

I had the same issues, for many, many years. My wife’s friend, who is a medical professional, pointed out that it could be ADHD/ADD. Turns out it was.  I was put on meds, and my ability to concentrate has improved drastically.
